Call Screening engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Call Screening capability in the binary covers storefront language. System telephony hooks, screening logic, and Connect actually separate call behavior from product-page copy:

  • Call Screening & unknown-caller flows — configured in your app or companion experience so unknown numbers are screened, callers may state a reason, and the user decides whether to answer. Controls in-app screening behavior. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • CallKit & CXProvider (different) — VoIP apps that report calls to the native incoming-call interface. See CallKit listing guide — engineering and marketing for native call UI, not screening-reason storefront copy.
  • Screened-call inbox & reason cards — in-app UI showing who called, what reason they gave, and accept-or-decline controls. Your listing may mention screening; building those views is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Carrier spam databases & third-party SDKs (different) — Hiya-style or Truecaller-style number lookup and network-level spam labels. Listing copy about screening should not overclaim universal carrier database coverage unless your app actually ships it.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of screening flags in the binary.

Working Call Screening in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Call Screening-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Screening-centric listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe unknown-caller screening — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Screen unknown callers vs generic "block spam"

US pages use "Call Screening", "Screen unknown callers", or "Ask why they're calling." Chinese buyers expect concise 来电筛选, 通话筛选, or 陌生来电筛选 phrasing — and copy that explains reason-before-ringing — rather than English slogans left on screenshot overlays. Avoid promising universal spam eradication when your app screens unknown numbers with a reason card.

Reason-before-ringing without carrier overclaims

Description and caption lines should name the screening flow your app actually supports — caller states a reason, user reviews before answer, screened-call inbox — without promising network-wide spam databases, unlimited PSTN blocking, or features your backend does not support. Common mistakes on Call Screening zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming screening support localizes automatically — Call Screening wired in Xcode; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screening screenshot caption lines still English
  • Conflating screening with Silence Unknown Callers — silencing unknown rings without a reason card is a different feature story on the product page
  • Conflating screening with CallKit VoIP UI — native incoming-call screens are CallKit marketing; reason-before-ringing cards are screening marketing
  • Conflating screening with Live Voicemail — transcription after a missed call is not pre-ring reason screening; see Live Voicemail listing guide
  • Claiming carrier-wide spam blocking — 全网拦截骚扰 or 运营商级防骚扰 overclaims when the app is a companion screener or reason inbox only
  • English "Screen unknown callers" on zh-Hans screenshots — Connect caption fields are Chinese but burned-in screening mockups on PNG exports are still Latin
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement Call Screening or CallKit — screening logic, CXProvider, and carrier SDK wiring are outside listing rewrite
